summary: Static census (name-level call graph, 188 fire roots incl. 73 merge fns, 27 adders found by fixpoint, callback parameters followed): 83 of 219 parameters are read in fire-reachable code (224 sites): 40 are assigned directly inside a function per command/file/registration, 23 only by parameterize, 9 at install/module level, 11 never; the power check finds all 5 current-source-loc reads and the worldview reads through maybe-wrap-worldview. On a persistent executor created once per process, 80-98 parameters are stale at every S0 round on the 26 corpus files that run S0 rounds, and 63-81 stay stale when the submitter's parameterization is captured and installed on wake, because call-with-parameterization does not carry direct assignments. A per-fire thread differential over 3,839 fires in 33 files (heavy, medium tier, speculation and NAF examples) finds 29 wrong fires on the persistent executor, with or without capture. All 29 are at one fire, the constraint-creation fire (typing-propagators.rkt:861), which writes constraint-top because it reads current-impl-registry through a default argument (constraint-propagators.rkt:55). Per-parameter re-binding attributes every divergence to that one parameter. Stale current-perf-counters also drops in-fire counts. On today's per-round threads, reads are correct by construction and measured so (0 stale, 0 divergent fires). The exposure there is on the write side only: lost direct assignments and read-modify-write races, shown on constructed power rows and not reached by the corpus. Printed results are identical on every leg (0/1,024), even under a worldview poison that changes 18 fires, so output-level parity cannot gate this; the gate must be fire-level.

verdicts.question: Q1 Static census: which parameters do S0 fire bodies read, directly or through production callees (parameter, defining site, assignment mode, reading fires)? Power check: current-source-loc's 5 reads and current-worldview-bitmask's reads through maybe-wrap-worldview.
verdicts.amendment: The census confirms CL-13's problem and amends D.2 §6.5 (D2:260-262) and the Q1 audit §6 (audit:496). D.2 says that, beyond the three fire-bound parameters, the ambient reads in S0 fires are the worldview, the retry-bridge box and the meta-solution callback. The census finds 83 parameters in fire-reachable code (over-approximate), and dynamic attribution adds two that D.2 does not list. (1) current-impl-registry, read by the constraint-creation fire typing-propagators.rkt:861/866 through the default argument of build-trait-constraint at constraint-propagators.rkt:55; it is the only parameter measured to change a fire's output. (2) current-perf-counters: its struct is read and mutated inside fires. The audit attributes the build-trait-constraint read to current-persistent-registry-net-box; the read is the parameter current-impl-registry, which is assigned directly (driver.rkt:3365 load-module; macros.rkt:8342 register-impl!), so the audit's 'stable if the box is the same on every executor' condition does not apply. C2-5 and C1-9 are confirmed: current-source-loc has 5 production reads and none of them emits an error inside a fire. 2 of them are fire-reachable only as #:srcloc defaults of in-fire installs (propagator.rkt:2289, :2372).
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. Command: racket census.rkt <worktree>/racket/prologos out (0.9 s; read-syntax, no expansion). Scope: 123 files (racket/prologos/*.rkt and lsp/*.rkt; tests, benchmarks, tools and examples excluded); 3,968 top-level defs; 219 parameters (equal to the 219 textual non-comment make-parameter lines). Fire roots: 188. 115 are fire functions, installed via net-add-propagator 63, net-add-fire-once-propagator 25, net-add-cross-domain-propagator 6, rt-add-propagator 6, rt-add-session-advance-in-rnet 4, elab-add-* 7, add-readiness-set-latch! 3 and module-network-install-fire-once 1. 73 are merge, contradicts? or widen functions (net-new-cell 45, register-merge-fn!/lattice 20, others 8), which run inside net-cell-write, inside the fire. Adders: 27, i.e. 7 primitives plus 20 wrappers found by fixpoint (a formal that flows into a fire argument, or is called inside an installed fire). Reach: 1,375 top-level defs, resolved by name and module through the require graph, with local binders excluded. Callback parameters dispatch to the functions assigned to them, including factory calls and callbacks the installer captured at install time. Result: 83 parameters, 224 read sites (out/census-summary.txt; full table out/census-params.tsv; witness paths out/census-paths.txt). Assignment modes (count, then key members and sites): (a) direct, inside a function: 40. Examples: the ~25 cell-id parameters and current-prop-meta-info-box (reset-meta-store! metavar-store.rkt:2850, 14 assignments at :2865-2909); init-meta-universes! (meta-universe.rkt:207-211); the registries in load-module (driver.rkt:3357-3368); register-impl!, register-trait! and register-subtype-pair! (macros.rkt:8342, :8279, :8036); current-relation-store (driver.rkt:1037). (b) parameterize only: 23. current-whnf-cache (driver.rkt:730), current-reduction-fuel, the nf and nat caches, current-perf-counters, current-worldview-bitmask (elab-speculation-bridge.rkt:298; relations.rkt:2087), current-source-loc, current-is-eval-fn, current-unify-depth. (c) install-time or module-level: 9. current-lattice-meta-solution-fn (driver.rkt:3865 -> type-lattice.rkt:69), current-constraint-retry-bridge-fn, the structural bridges, current-parallel-executor (driver.rkt:567). (d) never assigned: 11. Bound by the scheduler around each fire, hence thread-independent: current-bsp-fire-round? and current-cell-id-namespace (propagator.rkt:2884-2885); current-source-loc (:378); the worldview of fires wrapped by wrap-with-worldview (propagator.rkt:2175-2179) or maybe-wrap-worldview (relations.rkt:2082-2088). Reach is dominated by the reducer: typing and elaboration fires call whnf, and user-level network merges (reduction.rkt:4385-4396) evaluate Prologos code, so the relational and well-founded engines are statically reachable from S0.
verdicts.power_check: Finds all 5 current-source-loc reads (driver.rkt:681, elaborator.rkt:1149, propagator.rkt:2289, :2372, :2460) and its 3 binds (propagator.rkt:378, driver.rkt:681, elaborator.rkt:1149). Finds the worldview read inside maybe-wrap-worldview (relations.rkt:2083), its bind (:2087), and the fire-time read it feeds (net-cell-read, propagator.rkt:1601). Finds every Q1-audit §6 site: metavar-store.rkt:504; resolution.rkt:373 read and :386 set-box!; type-lattice.rkt:86. Version 1 of the census MISSED the retry bridge (out-v1/: the fire calls a function its installer read from current-constraint-retry-bridge-fn at metavar-store.rkt:1056). Following install-time captured callbacks fixed it: the method can fail, and the failure was found by this check. In the other direction, dyn3 re-bound all 219 parameters and found no fire depending on a parameter outside the static set.
verdicts.confidence: high for counts and sites; medium for completeness (callbacks stored in structs or registries, and match-pattern binders, are approximated)

verdicts.question: Q2(a) Which of those parameters would hold a stale or wrong value on a persistent executor created once per process (C6-2)?
verdicts.amendment: (1) The triage's interim fix does not suffice. That fix captures the per-run parameterization and installs it on each wake. It carries parameterize bindings but not direct assignments: it fixes 12 of the 42 stale fire-read parameters and leaves 30 stale. Among those 30 is current-impl-registry, the only parameter measured to change a fire's write (29 fires in 6 of 33 files, identical with and without capture). (2) The defect sits at cell level and does not show in printed results (0 of 1,024 differ on any leg), so a parity or suite gate on outputs cannot detect it. (3) On the corpus the measured damage is one fire family plus one counter. Most stale values (cell ids, registries, network boxes) are never read in a way that changes a fire. The blocker therefore holds for 'persistent executor plus ambient reads', but the work it implies is small and specific. Fix shape: remove the read from the fire. Pass the impl registry as data, or read it on the topology tier; build-trait-constraint already takes it as an explicit argument 'to avoid parameter coupling' (constraint-propagators.rkt:53-55), and the caller at typing-propagators.rkt:866 omits it. Keep counters out of fires. Run nested quiescence inline on the executor's own thread. Gate with the fire-level differential (W2-5-1).
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. Legs (dyn.rkt, one process per file and leg, 33 files): seq; fresh (one new #:pool 'own thread per round); prod (make-parallel-thread-fire-all); persist (one thread created after module load and before process-file, reused); persistcap (persist, with each job run under call-with-parameterization of the submitter's current parameterization). Staleness compares all 219 parameters with eq? and equal? at every round. Persist: 80-98 parameters not equal? to the submitter's value on the 26 files with S0 rounds (103 distinct). The executor sees current-prop-net-box #f, current-impl-registry #hasheq(), cell ids #f, empty registries. Persistcap: 63-81 per file (84 distinct). Of the 83 static fire-read parameters, 42 are stale on persist and 30 on persistcap. Capture fixes current-whnf-cache, nf-cache, nat-value-cache, reduction-fuel, prop-net-box, perf-counters, provenance-counters, quiescence-stats, is-eval-fn, unify-depth, source-loc and parallel-executor. dyn2.rkt fires each round's pids against the same snapshot on main twice (R1, plus R2 as a control) and once on the executor (RX), and continues with R1. Over 3,839 executor-dispatched fires: persist 29 thread-divergent fires, persistcap 29, fresh 0; control-divergent 0. All 29 are typing-propagators.rkt:861. First diff: path (fire-result value-writes, cell 49, dict meta, :constraints); main writes constraint-set{Eq Bool, Eq Posit16, ...}, the executor writes constraint-top. Per file: type-adversarial 15, solve-carrier 5, constraints-adversarial 4, punify-acceptance 2, track8-acceptance 2, ppn-track4c-adversarial 1. dyn3.rkt re-binds each stale parameter alone to the value a thread created at harness start holds: only current-impl-registry changes any fire, with the same counts. Perf counters: the driver's per-file PERF-COUNTERS reduce_steps, seq to persist: 1143->1049 (constraints-adversarial), 2478->2383 (type-adversarial), 59->58 (simple-typed); equal on persistcap. The in-fire increments land on #f. Worldview: read in fires (the dyn3 poison row changes 18 fires in 3 files, at relations.rkt:2840, a producer that maybe-wrap-worldview left unwrapped at bm=0, and at discrim-fire, relations.rkt:778). It was never stale at round entry on this corpus, because no S0 round ran under a nonzero ambient bitmask. It is latent through elab-speculation-bridge.rkt:298 and through maybe-wrap-worldview's install-time read (relations.rkt:2083) in in-fire installs. Re-entrancy: 0 nested executor calls in 3,839 fires. Static paths from fires to run-to-quiescence exist (retry bridge -> unify.rkt:340, :392, :432), so a single persistent executor that submits to itself would deadlock. power.rkt P2: (a) persistent, plain: the fire saw 'at-load after main's direct assignment; (b) with captured parameterization: still 'at-load; (c) a parameterize binding is captured; (d) a fresh thread sees the assignment. This matches C6's own p1-semantics.out line 13 (q-at-load under main's captured parameterization) and Racket Reference §11.3.2: a direct assignment 'changes the value in the current thread cell'.
verdicts.power_check: Negative control: the fresh leg of the same harness gives 0 divergent fires and 0 stale parameters. Positive rows: the dyn3 WV-POISON row flags 18 fires (atms-adversarial, c2-naf, parity-adversarial). The known current-impl-registry case is flagged by both dyn2 and dyn3. control-divergent = 0 in every run, so nondeterministic fires do not pollute the differential. Not covered: fires that bypass current-parallel-executor (Tier-1 flush propagator.rkt:3441; drain :2775; widen and narrow :4162, :4227). The retry bridge and the solve-meta box writes are not reached by this corpus (dyn4: 0 box writes during fires in 33 files, with a power row).

verdicts.question: Q2(b)-reads Which parameters would hold a stale or wrong value on today's thread-per-round executor (make-parallel-thread-fire-all, driver.rkt:567)?
verdicts.amendment: None. C6-2's stale-value hazard does not apply to threads created per round. On today's executor the exposure is on the write side only (next verdict).
verdicts.evidence: THEOREM. A thread created by `thread` starts with its creator's current parameterization and its creator's current values of preserved thread cells; parameters are preserved cells (Racket Reference §11.3.2 Parameters; Evaluation Model, thread cells). Hypotheses: (H1) each round's threads are created inside the executor call (propagator.rkt:3715, called from :3497) by the thread that holds the round's dynamic context, after its last assignment; (H2) that thread assigns nothing until it has joined them (it blocks in channel-get at :3726). Under H1 and H2, every parameter read in the round sees the value the sequential executor would see. MEASUREMENT: dynA fresh leg: 0 parameters stale (eq?) at any round, 33 files, all 219 compared. dyn2 fresh: 0 thread-divergent fires of 3,839. Printed results equal on fresh and prod for 33 files (1,024 results, gensym and meta counters normalised).
verdicts.power_check: On the persist leg the same instrument reports 80-98 stale parameters per file and dyn2 reports 29 divergent fires, so it can see staleness. power.rkt P2(d) shows a fresh thread picking up a direct assignment that a persistent thread misses.

verdicts.question: Q2(b)-writes Do any fires assign parameters, or set-box! shared boxes, whose effects a per-round thread would lose or race on?
verdicts.amendment: Statically yes; on the corpus no. The exposure is real by construction and latent in the corpus. It becomes live when one of these runs in a wide round (>= 8 fires): (a) the retry bridge or a solve-meta path, which writes the shared elaboration-network box from two threads (lost update); (b) an enabled counting instrument (verbose perf counters, subtype counting), whose counts then become nondeterministic; (c) a user-level network that evaluates solve inside a fire, which assigns current-wf-table-store and current-naf-deferred? on a thread that then dies. Separately, an exception raised in a fire on today's executor kills its thread and leaves channel-get at propagator.rkt:3726 blocked (C6 p1 EXC): the exception is lost, not just a value.
verdicts.evidence: Static (census): 9 fire-reachable direct assignments to 7 parameters: subtype-predicate.rkt:77 current-subtype-check-count; metavar-store.rkt:2038 current-bvar-solution-count; wf-engine.rkt:145 and :200 current-naf-deferred?; wf-engine.rkt:450 and :485 current-wf-table-store; cfa-analysis.rkt:290; confluence-analysis.rkt:70; termination-analysis.rkt:76. All are reached through the reducer or relational engine, or gated by a counter that defaults to #f. Shared writes in fire-reachable code: set-box! of the elaboration-network box reached through current-prop-net-box (resolution.rkt:386 retry bridge; metavar-store.rkt:1002-1066 add-constraint!; :1326; :2006; :2075-2108 solve-meta-core!; :2211; :2500; :2628; unify.rkt:342, :393, :433), and of the meta-info box (metavar-store.rkt:2078). Read-modify-write counters: subtype-predicate.rkt:81 and :83 (module boxes); perf-counter fields (performance-counters.rkt:183-258, via current-perf-counters); quiescence counters (propagator.rkt:1903, :1935, :2033). Memo tables: loose-bvar.rkt:111, macros.rkt:8093, reduction.rkt:4831, ctor-registry.rkt:156, and the whnf, nf and nat caches (reduction.rkt:2759, :4954, :1129, the first under driver.rkt:730). hash-set! takes the table's semaphore per Racket's hash-table concurrency caveats; hash-ref! and hash-update! are not atomic, which costs only duplicate work for pure memos. Dynamic: 0 of 219 parameters changed by fires on the executor thread (dynA, all legs, 33 files, 3,839 fires). 0 box writes during fires to current-prop-net-box, current-prop-meta-info-box and current-persistent-registry-net-box (dyn4, 33 files). Perf counters identical, seq vs prod, on both heavy files.
verdicts.power_check: power.rkt P1: 16 fires that each assign current-subtype-check-count. Under seq the main thread then sees (16 . 0); under a fresh thread and under the production executor it sees (0 . 0): the assignments are lost. P3: 64 fires x 2,000 read-modify-write increments of one shared box under make-parallel-thread-fire-all: 9 runs over 3 processes gave 117,910 / 119,735 / 116,940 / 111,927 / 109,417 / 124,614 / 106,346 / 94,097 / 92,000 of 128,000 (3-28 % lost); seq exact. The dyn4 POWER row flags a synthetic fire's set-box!. P4: the re-entrancy counter sees 3 nested calls from 3 fires.
verdicts.confidence: high for the static list and the dynamic zero; medium for the latent reach

verdicts.question: Q3 Confirm the top candidates dynamically with no rebuild: injected executors (sequential; fresh thread per round; one thread created earlier and reused) on the heavy files and speculation-heavy examples.
verdicts.amendment: Of the 83 static candidates, 3 are confirmed as read inside S0 fires in a way that matters: current-impl-registry (wrong value, ⊤ written), current-perf-counters (stale, counts lost) and current-worldview-bitmask (read, output-relevant under poison, not stale on the corpus). The rest are stale, or reachable, without a measured effect on the corpus, which says nothing about programs outside it. The amendment is about method: comparing printed results has no power here. Use the fire-level differential and the per-parameter attribution, both injected through current-parallel-executor.
verdicts.evidence: Corpus: 33 files. 19 benchmarks/comparative, including both heavy files. 10 examples: wfle-acceptance, bsp-le-track2, propagator-demo, ppn-track4c-adversarial, relational-demo, narrowing-demo, sudoku-demo, solve-carrier, punify-acceptance, track8-acceptance. 4 wave-1 C9 probes (c1-overwrite, c2-naf, c3-naf-nested, c4-varvar). In total 1,040 BSP rounds, 107 wide (>= 8), 3,839 executor-dispatched fires. Results: printed results equal on every leg after normalising gensym and meta counters (normcmp.py, 0 of 1,024 differ). dyn2: thread-divergent fires fresh 0, persist 29, persistcap 29. dyn3: only current-impl-registry; WV-POISON 18. PERF-COUNTERS reduce_steps lower on persist only. Even the deliberate worldview poison (wvpoison leg: bit 60 on the worker) leaves printed results unchanged on atms-adversarial, c2-naf and solve-adversarial, while it changes 18 fire outputs.
verdicts.power_check: Positive and negative rows as in Q2(a): fresh 0 against persist 29; WV-POISON 18; control-divergent 0. Separately, the output comparison was shown to have no power (0 diffs under poison), which is why the verdict rests on the fire-level instruments.

findings.claim_attacked: That a green full suite or parity suite at K = 1 and K > 1 (with the replay monitor) is evidence that executors preserve fire context.
findings.evidence: On a persistent executor, 29 fires write constraint-top into the :constraints facet instead of a candidate set, yet 0 of 1,024 printed results differ across 33 files. A deliberately wrong worldview on the worker changes 18 fire outputs in 3 files and 0 printed results. The suite checks outputs, so it has no power on this class. D.2's replay monitor compares cells, so it would see the ⊤ only if its replay runs with the submitter's ambient state; D.2 does not say on which thread the replay runs.
findings.direction: Add a fire-context differential to the gates. It is a cell, not a scheduler mode: for each epoch, a monitor propagator-set re-fires the epoch's fires against x⁰ₑ on the submitting thread, with a determinism control, and compares them with the executor's fire results. A per-parameter attribution pass (re-bind one parameter at a time to its creation-time value) names the culprit. Both need no rebuild (current-parallel-executor). This is the 'census trap for parameter reads at K > 1' the triage asks for. State that the replay runs on the submitting thread.
findings.falsifier: A suite test that fails on the persistent-executor constraint-top write, or an output-level gate row with a demonstrated power row on this class.

findings.section: D.2 §6.5 (D2:260-262); Q1 audit §6 row current-persistent-registry-net-box (audit:496); P0 §9.5
findings.claim_attacked: That the ambient reads left in S0 fires are the worldview, the retry-bridge box and current-lattice-meta-solution-fn, all removed by the merge and fire rows; and that build-trait-constraint's registry read is stable on every executor.
findings.evidence: The one ambient read measured to change a fire is not in D.2's list. The constraint-creation fire (typing-propagators.rkt:860-868, installed at :2586) calls (build-trait-constraint trait-name) at :866 without its registry argument, so the default (current-impl-registry) at constraint-propagators.rkt:55 is read inside the fire. current-impl-registry (macros.rkt:8320) is a parameter, assigned directly in load-module (driver.rkt:3365) and in register-impl! (macros.rkt:8342). It is not the persistent-registry box. A persistent executor sees #hasheq() and writes constraint-top: 29 fires in 6 of 33 files, with and without a captured parameterization (dyn2, dyn3). current-perf-counters is also read and mutated in fires (reduce_steps lost on persist: 1143->1049, 2478->2383).
findings.direction: Give the fire its registry as data. Either the installer, on the topology tier, passes the registry value (or the registry cell id it already allocates: current-impl-registry-cell-id) into make-constraint-creation-fire-fn, or the fire reads the registry cell. Delete the default-argument read. Keep perf counters out of fire bodies; count per epoch from the epoch record. Add these rows to D.2 §6.5's inventory and fix the audit row.
findings.falsifier: dyn3 rerun with the registry passed explicitly still showing a divergent fire at typing-propagators.rkt:861.

findings.claim_attacked: That printed results are reproducible run to run under one executor, so that a parity or replay comparison can diff them directly.
findings.evidence: Three runs under the sequential executor print different gensym suffixes in the same result. atms-adversarial result 114: c_g2446, c_g2449, c_g2448. solve-adversarial result 60: c_g2060, c_g2060, c_g2059. The first harness comparison flagged these as differences until the suffixes were normalised.
findings.direction: Compare modulo gensym and meta-counter renaming in any parity or replay that reads printed results. Finding the source of the varying gensym count (CONJECTURE: iteration over address-keyed tables, or GC-timing-dependent paths) is a reproducibility item for W2-10.
findings.falsifier: Ten consecutive sequential runs that print identical suffixes.
